title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

reading.body:
The incident involves synthetic or fabricated pornographic material being created and distributed under a real person's identity without her knowledge or consent. The impersonation extended beyond static images to include a fabricated sex video, and the person responsible is alleged to have monetised access to that material over a period of years. This places the harm at the intersection of non-consensual intimate imagery and identity fraud conducted through online platforms.

The title of the report introduces a specific allegation: that the person responsible was Fernandes's husband. That allegation is reported by Fernandes herself and is not established as a legal finding. No conviction, admission, or court ruling is described in the available reporting.

What the incident illustrates as a failure mode is the use of digital tools to fabricate and circulate sexualised content depicting a real, named individual, combined with sustained impersonation for the purpose of conducting false relationships and extracting payment. The fabrication went undetected by Fernandes for years, and she identified the responsible party through her own investigation rather than through any platform or legal mechanism. Whether the platforms hosting or distributing the material had any detection systems in place, and whether those systems were active, is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

summary:
German actress and television personality Collien Fernandes discovered that someone was impersonating her online and conducting sexually explicit affairs with men using her name. The imposter had been creating and sharing pornographic material purportedly featuring her for years, sometimes charging men for access. After learning about a fabricated sex video in 2021, Fernandes decided to investigate her harassers herself rather than ignore the problem. Through considerable effort, she identified one person she believed was responsible for the impersonation.

Fernandes was a high-profile figure in Germany who had been married to actor and comedian Christian Ulmen for 14 years before their divorce. During their marriage, the couple was known for their feminist values, and Fernandes had published children's books and produced documentaries about gender issues. On a March evening while filming in Vietnam, Fernandes prepared to publicly expose the person she had identified as her imposter, an action that would eventually spark a broader feminist movement.
